html:
The Spanish Civil War began in July 1936 when army officers rose against the elected government of the Second Republic. It ended in April 1939 with the victory of the Nationalists under General Francisco Franco.

The Republic was backed by the left, the unions and the Basque and Catalan regions, the Nationalists by the army, the Church, monarchists and the Falange. Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy sent troops, planes and arms to Franco; the Soviet Union aided the Republic, and thousands of foreign volunteers joined the International Brigades. Britain and France stayed out.

German planes destroyed the Basque town of Guernica in 1937, recalled in Picasso's painting. The siege of Madrid lasted almost the whole war. About half a million people died, many in killings behind the lines, and hundreds of thousands fled into exile. Franco ruled until his death in 1975. See Spain.
sum: The Spanish Civil War began in July 1936 when army officers rose against the elected government of the Second Republic. It ended in April 1939 with the victory of the Nationalists under General Francisco Franco.
